messages:
emily.ops: paging: multiple customers reporting outbound timeouts and 504s from hosted inference in eu-west-2. Endpoint logs show CONNECT timeout to external model-registry and some hosts failing healthchecks. Notifying oncall.
incbot: @ajay-oncall alerted (pager duty). Incident channel created. Severity: P2.
raj.sre: jumping in — are we seeing region-wide or AZ-scoped?
emily.ops: early signs point to AZ-b.. metrics: NAT egress bytes dropped, route table flaps noted in cloud logs. Only services with outbound to internet affected, internal intra-vpc still OK.
sarah-net: pulling VPC flow logs now. Looks like source port 1024-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0 timed out from subnets in az-b-2. I also see a spike in NACL denies around 3505000120.
ajay-oncall: confirmed I'm oncall. Can you paste the last terraform apply or API call history for networking?
emily.ops: checking — there was an automated security rollout by infra-control-plane at 3504999950 that updated a handful of SGs and one NACL. policy-id: rollout-2026-03-15-net.
raj.sre: that aligns. I see route-update events: one route table in az-b had a transient replacement of the default route to a stale NAT instance (terminated) at ~3505000055. That would blackhole egress.
sarah-net: interesting — NACL denies + stale NAT route could explain partial egress. Which subnets are on that route table?
emily.ops: subnets app-eu-west-2b-1 and batch-eu-west-2b-2. Those host customers' batched inference jobs.
ajay-oncall: impact: customer background jobs failing, real-time API latency increased for clients pinned to az-b. Any customer-facing alerts?
emily.ops: support page shows spike in error tickets for embeddings and async jobs starting ~3505000080. Estimated affected customer set: ~8 tenants, partial degradation (timeouts 10-30s, retries).
raj.sre: mitigation plan: 1) revert NACL change if present 2) update route table to point to healthy managed NAT gateway 3) if NAT instance still in TF state, detach/replace 4) re-run healthchecks and validate flows. Who can roll back infra-control-plane?
emily.ops: @sarah-net you have permissions to revert the NACL and re-associate a stable route target?
sarah-net: on it. Reverting NACL now. Command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 100 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow --egress
```
(sorry shorthand). Replaced deny with allow for ephemeral egress.
raj.sre: while that's happening I'll update the route table. Route currently points to eni-terminated-abc. Setting route to nat-0healthy123. Command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0xdeadbeef --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0healthy123
```
Applied.
emily.ops: deploy-bot: did the infra-control-plane run any canary? deploying?
deploy-bot: rollout-2026-03-15-net completed; automation triggered by schedule. Change set: sg and nacl updates across eu-west-2. No canary blocking.
ajay-oncall: ok, confirm route replacement succeeded and start synthetic checks.
sarah-net: flow logs show allowed egress after 3505000200 for many flows, but some connections still SACKing due to conntrack stale entries on the NAT gateway.
raj.sre: forcing conntrack flush on NAT gateway by toggling target in the managed pool. Steps: detach ENI, reattach new nat interface. Doing it now.
emily.ops: customers reporting gradual recovery — some jobs requeued and now succeeding. Support posted update to customers at 3505000305.
ajay-oncall: handoff note for oncall: I will stay until handover in 30m to ensure no regression. Primary mitigations done: NACL revert, route fixed to healthy NAT, forced conntrack reset.
raj.sre: follow-up actions: 1) add pre-check guard in infra-control-plane to detect any route pointing to terminated ENI 2) add canary subset in az-b for NACL/SG rollouts 3) tighten automated rollback for route changes 4) run postmortem with infra-control-plane team.
sarah-net: uploading logs and commands to the incident ticket. Also adding a rule to block automation from touching route tables unless canary passes.
emily.ops: customer impact summary for the postmortem draft: duration ~15m severe egress timeouts for a subset of az-b subnets; partial customer impact for ~8 tenants, mostly batch/async jobs — realtime endpoints degraded for clients pinned to az-b; no data loss, retries and requeues mitigated.
ajay-oncall: creating RCA draft. tagging: #networking #egress #automation-rollout.
emily.ops: thanks everyone. leaving handoff at 3505000487 to @raj.sre for follow-up; @ajay-oncall please escalate to infra-control-plane owners and schedule postmortem meeting. :thumbsup:
